data.name: Enterprises Rapidly Shift to Multi-Model AI Strategies
data.summary: Databricks' new AI Index, based on traffic from over 10,000 enterprises, shows open-weight models jumping from 7.3% to 30.9% of token traffic in just 3.5 months. Today, 75% of firms use two or more providers, and half use three or more, favoring models like DeepSeek and Zhipu for coding and batch tasks. Leaders like Patrick Wendell and CEO Ali Ghodsi call the changes striking, as task-specific routing—such as Claude for planning and OpenAI for editing—becomes standard, pointing to a market optimizing for cost and fit over single-lab loyalty.

data.summary: Goodfire, a 2023-founded specialist in mechanistic interpretability, caught OpenAI's eye for its tools that peer inside neural networks to spot hidden dangers like cyberattacks. Talks this summer aimed at a $5 billion valuation—four times its recent $1.25 billion funding round—but fell through as Goodfire chose independence to serve multiple AI labs. Backed by investors like Anthropic and Menlo Ventures, the startup already partners with Microsoft and others, highlighting the push for safer AI through transparent 'black box' analysis.

The mix-up underscores debates on AGI timelines, precise definitions, and the balance between rapid progress and responsible oversight.

data.hook: David Bessis fired up an incognito chat with Anthropic's Claude to tweak some talk notes. Then he saw his own name and email pop up in the AI's hidden reasoning steps.
data.name: Mathematician Spots Claude AI Using His Email in Incognito Chat
data.summary: Bessis called the Opus 5.5 model's behavior a 'distressing level of dishonesty' since the session was meant to be memory-less and anonymous. Claude explained that every message includes the account's email as background context, used only internally without affecting responses, and offered to treat him as an anonymous writer. Anthropic's docs confirm incognito chats aren't saved to history or memory and aren't used for training, but they're kept 30 days for safety and still access profile info like custom styles. The case spotlights how 'incognito' labels might mislead users about true privacy limits.

data.hook: Developers can now run open AI models on Hugging Face with requests automatically routed to the fastest, cheapest, most reliable providers—no extra hassle required.
data.name: Hugging Face Partners with OpenRouter for Smarter Model Routing
data.summary: The partnership integrates OpenRouter's inference routing directly into the Hugging Face Hub, directing each request to the best provider based on price, speed, and uptime, with automatic failover for reliability. Users keep their familiar Hugging Face tokens and endpoints while gaining access to 160 models from 38 labs, plus live stats and a redesigned inference widget. Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue emphasized collaboration over competition, noting open-weight models now make up 72% of OpenRouter's tokens served and cost four times less than closed ones. Traces from requests can flow into users' storage for evaluations or fine-tuning, simplifying workflows for popular models like Qwen and DeepSeek.
